samples.summary: `writePageSetup` still writes through the raw `docStore`, the one editor write path left outside the new disposal revocation
samples.evidence: The diff routes `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:3356) through `revocableStore` precisely so a disposed handle has no page-setup-shaped hole, but its twin `writePageSetup` — the shared implementation driven by BOTH `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` and the ruler's margin drag (`ruler.onMarginChange`, editor.ts:2367) — still calls `docStore.snapshot()` / `docStore.setPageSetup(...)` on the RAW store at editor.ts:2357-2360. Today this is unreachable after `dispose()` only by accident of ordering: `api.setPageSetup` is in `MUTATING_METHODS`, and `ruler.dispose()` (packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:460) removes the document-level mousemove/mouseup handlers inside the same synchronous `dispose()`. Any new or async caller of `writePageSetup` would write through a revoked editor. The fix belongs on the new code: point `writePageSetup` at `revocableStore` too.

samples.summary: The depth-based undo floor this change replaced as wrong in `YorkieDocStore` is still in use, unchanged, in the notes, slides and board stores
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.canUndo()` was reworked (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3085-3136) on the stated grounds that comparing `getUndoStackForTest().length` against a load-time depth stops being correct the moment Yorkie's 50-entry cap `shift()`s entries off the bottom (#1045), refusing undos that are still reachable. The three sibling stores keep exactly the replaced form: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:374` (`getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`), `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:667`, `packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:514` — the last two even comment that they 'mirror YorkieDocStore', which is now false. Pre-existing behaviour, but the three are now out of step with the store they say they copy and with the comment block that documents the rule.

samples.summary: `SharedDocumentByToken`'s two template-preview consumers silently inherit the new 60-second poll and the new 'a verdict closes the view' eviction
samples.evidence: The component was rewritten from a one-shot `useEffect` resolve into a `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` and `isShareLinkResolveFatal` eviction (shared-document.tsx:1057-1115). Its other two mount sites are template previews — `packages/frontend/src/app/templates/template-landing.tsx:174` and `packages/frontend/src/app/templates/template-review-queue.tsx:136` — neither of which is a live-capability surface. They now issue one unauthenticated resolve per minute per open preview against a globally throttled endpoint (120 req/min/IP, app.module.ts:102), and an open preview whose token is rotated or expires will now tear itself down to a 'Link unavailable' panel mid-view, where before it stayed rendered. Both consumers are inside App.tsx's QueryClientProvider, so nothing crashes; the change is behavioural.

samples.summary: The hunt bridge's `doc.canUndo` oracle documents MemDocStore's old eager-snapshot semantics
samples.evidence: `bridge.ts:376` tells agent callers that `MemDocStore` has 'real snapshot-based undo/redo stacks', and `doc.canUndo` (bridge.ts:386) reads `editor.getStore().canUndo()`. After this change `snapshot()` records a pending checkpoint instead of pushing (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts), so an action that snapshots and writes nothing no longer makes `canUndo()` true — the harness's own test files needed exactly this fixup (see `packages/docs/test/view/caret-line-affinity.test.ts`'s new `undoableEdit` helper). Any hunt oracle phrased as 'the action ran, so undo is available' now answers differently. The harness lane is not run by CI, so nothing will flag it.
